text.text_excerpt: The Pupusa Lady has been on my list for quite some time, and after making pupusas of my own for the first time, I figured it was time to taste the real deal. These traditional pockets of deliciousness did not disappoint. I had a cheese and pork stuffed one in addition to one that was stuffed with cheese and edible flowers, I believe it was called the Loroca. I was curious how the edible flowers would taste, but this was definitely my favorite one. They are huge and served with a pickled cabbage slaw. I hope this place never leaves Roux Carre-it's such a cool spot! I will be back to have more delicious pupusas!

I thought I had experienced papusas before but now I realize I hadn't. YUM ! I think I could get addicted. Also the shrimp ceviche was divine and came with a crown of popcorn! I thought that was odd but when you taste it together it makes perfect sense. The collection of restaurants here at the ROUX CARRE all look inviting, I will comeback to try the others.

Cute little family-operated booth in Roux Carre. They have classic papusas, but when I went they had a special "mardi gras" purple (beets), green (kale), and gold (crawfish) setup. All of them were delicious! The horchata was really flavorful as well. My only sorrow was that they were out of maduros plantains. Note to future self: they a special brunch menu that includes baleadas.
